ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Sugar Ray Robinson Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Establishing care for memory loss and getting lost, with his care partner: cognitive testing, reversible causes, medicines, diabetes and blood pressure, driving and firearm safety. Concerns: He wants to know why he is forgetting and what can be done; He wants to keep his independence and keep working with the young fighters at the foundation; His care partner is worried about his driving and about managing alone. [S]

MRI of the brain without contrast, with susceptibility-weighted imaging: moderate atrophy of both hippocampi, left more than right (medial temporal atrophy score 2 on each side), mild generalized atrophy, a few small white matter hyperintensities (Fazekas 1), six microbleeds at the gray-white junction of both frontal lobes and the right temporal lobe in a pattern seen after traumatic brain injury, no cortical superficial siderosis, no infarct, mass or hydrocephalus, and a cavum septi pellucidi, a finding common in boxers
Pure tone audiometry: mild to moderate bilateral high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, symmetric; speech understanding good in quiet, reduced in noise
Amyloid PET with florbetapir: positive, with widespread cortical tracer uptake (about 90 Centiloids), confirming Alzheimer's disease pathology
Twelve-lead ECG before donepezil: sinus rhythm at 70 per minute, PR interval 172 ms, QTc 414 ms, no conduction block
Fitting of hearing aids for both ears by the audiologist, with teaching for him and his care partner
Advance care planning conversation, about 30 minutes, with him and his care partner; his capacity to name a health care agent and state his values was assessed and present
Twelve-lead ECG: sinus bradycardia at 56 per minute, PR interval 180 ms, QTc 420 ms, no heart block

tr.td: Establishing care for memory loss and getting lost, with his care partner: cognitive testing, reversible causes, medicines, diabetes and blood pressure, driving and firearm safety
Two-week review, seen the same day by cognitive neurology: brain MRI, hearing test, staging, Alzheimer's disease against traumatic encephalopathy syndrome, and anti-amyloid eligibility
Six-week review: amyloid PET result, the diagnosis and the plan, with diabetes, driving, firearm and caregiver support
Eleven-week review: donepezil dose, diabetes, hearing aids and day program
Sixteen-week review: medicines, kidneys, mood, caregiver strain and the plan
Same-day sick visit for nausea and dizziness on donepezil

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Dementia work-up under the Alzheimer's Association guideline: history from him and his care partner, MoCA, function, depression screening, first-tier blood tests (blood count, metabolic panel, B12, TSH), a review of medicines for anticholinergic and sedating drugs, a sleep apnea screen, and brain MRI

Cognitive neurology consultation at the memory clinic to stage the dementia, weigh Alzheimer's disease against traumatic encephalopathy syndrome and vascular disease, choose biomarker testing, and decide anti-amyloid eligibility
Stop diphenhydramine, a strongly anticholinergic sleep aid; sleep habits and morning light instead
Driving: no driving until the evaluation is complete, with his care partner driving; firearm: unloaded and locked, with the key held by his care partner, until a decision with him
Amyloid PET to confirm Alzheimer's disease pathology; APOE genotyping not needed because he is not a candidate for anti-amyloid therapy, and offered only with counseling
Donepezil 5 mg at bedtime with a baseline ECG and pulse checks, raised to 10 mg after four to six weeks if tolerated; taken in the morning if dreams are vivid

Diabetes deintensified under the ADA Standards for older adults: stop glipizide, continue metformin, hemoglobin A1c goal under 8.0%, sick-day rules (hold metformin when not eating or drinking), and B12 checked periodically
Blood pressure under 130/80 mmHg on lisinopril, with potassium and creatinine checks
Hearing aids for both ears, fitted by the audiologist
Stop driving after the diagnosis (CDR 1 and getting lost), with transport planned; the handgun removed from the home
Caregiver support: education, the Alzheimer's Association 24/7 Helpline, an adult day program for respite, a caregiver burden check, and the Medicare GUIDE dementia care model once he has Medicare
Advance care planning while he can take part fully: a health care agent and his values, at the preventive visit
Exercise, social activity and diabetes and blood pressure control as the brain-health measures with the most support
Find the cause of the memory loss and explain it to him in a way he can take in
Alzheimer's disease confirmed by amyloid PET; disclosed with his care partner present, at his request, with written notes
No hypoglycemia, with hemoglobin A1c under 8.0%
Glipizide stopped after one reading of 68 mg/dL; no low readings since; A1c 6.4 to 6.9%
Stay safe: no driving and no firearm in the home
He stopped driving and the handgun was removed from the home
Keep his days full and give his care partner regular breaks
Adult day program two days a week; walks and the foundation gym on other days; Alzheimer's Association helpline

list.item: Independent in bathing, dressing, eating and walking; needs help with bills, medicines and appointments (Functional Activities Questionnaire 11, narrative); Timed Up and Go 9 seconds [S]

Alert, cheerful and courteous; repeats a question twice in ten minutes; looks to his care partner for dates; speech fluent; mood good; no hallucinations or delusions; insight partial: he notices forgetting but feels it is normal for his age [S]
